name: Çatalhöyük
place: the Konya plain of central Anatolia
desc: One of the first towns: thousands of people in mud-brick houses packed wall to wall with no streets, coming and going over the rooftops by ladder. They painted bulls and vultures on their walls, set horns in the plaster, buried their dead under the floors and made the first mirrors of polished obsidian.
source: Excavations by James Mellaart (1961–65) and Ian Hodder (1993–2017); a UNESCO World Heritage site

cautious: replastered the house white for the fortieth time
devout: painted a great red bull on the north wall
gluttonous: filled the clay bins with lentils for the winter

inventions.name: Rooftop Town
inventions.source: Çatalhöyük's houses stood wall to wall with no streets; people walked over the roofs and entered by ladders through the smoke hole
inventions.desc: Houses packed so close that the outer walls make one great wall, with the doors on the roofs: +2 defence, the cold bites 10% less.
inventions.hint: Comes from building and the hearth.

inventions.name: Obsidian Mirrors
inventions.source: Polished obsidian mirrors from Çatalhöyük graves, about 8,000 years old, the oldest mirrors known
inventions.desc: Black volcanic glass ground and polished until it shows a face: +2 mood, a little more lore.

inventions.name: Plastered Bull Horns
inventions.source: Horns of wild aurochs were set in plaster benches and pillars inside the houses
inventions.desc: The horns of the great wild bulls set into the walls, to keep their strength in the house: rites bring 10% more devotion, +1 attack.
inventions.hint: Comes from hunting and the rites.

inventions.name: Fresh White Plaster
inventions.source: Some house walls at Çatalhöyük were replastered more than a hundred times, perhaps every year
inventions.desc: Walls and floors coated again and again with clean white clay: the sick recover 10% faster, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Comes from building and the hearth.

inventions.name: Wall Paintings
inventions.source: Paintings of bull hunts, vultures and a town plan beneath a twin-peaked mountain, perhaps the volcano Hasan Dağ
inventions.desc: Red and black paintings of the hunt, the dead and the mountain on the white walls: +3 mood.

foods.name: Wheat and Lentil Stew
foods.source: Çatalhöyük grew emmer, einkorn, barley, peas and lentils, and stored them in clay bins inside the houses
foods.desc: Wheat and lentils simmered in a clay oven: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Hackberry Paste
foods.source: Hackberry seeds are among the commonest plant remains at Çatalhöyük
foods.desc: Sweet little berries pounded with their stones into a paste that keeps: +2 mood, food spoils 5% slower.

finds.name: Obsidian of the Twin Mountain
finds.source: Obsidian from the volcanoes of Cappadocia, Hasan Dağ and Göllü Dağ
finds.desc: Black volcanic glass that breaks into the sharpest edges.

finds.name: Hackberry Trees
finds.desc: Trees with small sweet berries and very hard stones.

people.name: Kerpic
people.desc: Every spring she makes every house in the row white again.
memory: plastered over the old painting and began a new one

people.name: Boğa
people.desc: He was in the painting of the bull hunt, teasing its tail.
memory: grabbed the tail of a wild bull and lived

people.name: The Seated Woman
people.source: A clay figurine of a heavy woman seated between two leopards, found in a grain bin in 1961 (Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, Ankara)
people.desc: An old woman of great size, her hands resting on two leopards: a goddess to some, an honoured elder to others.

people.name: The Painter of the Mountain
people.source: A wall painting of houses beneath a twin-peaked mountain, read by some as the oldest map and an eruption of Hasan Dağ
people.desc: An unknown artist who painted the town's houses, and above them a mountain with two peaks, perhaps spitting fire.

people.name: Kara Taş
people.text: a trader who comes down from the volcano with black glass, and climbs in through the roof like everyone else.
memory: chipped a hundred blades from one block of black glass
people.desc: An obsidian trader of the kind who supplied Çatalhöyük.

people.name: Pars
people.label: Pars, Mother of Leopards
people.desc: She sits between leopards and they obey her. Lore 8, Foraging 5.

people.name: Dam
people.label: Dam, Builder of the Rooftops
people.desc: His houses fit together like the cells of a honeycomb. Crafting 8.

people.name: Yaban Boğa
people.label: Yaban Boğa, Who Teases the Wild Bull
people.desc: He leaps around the great bull until it tires. Combat 8.

events.title: Beneath the Floor
events.source: At Çatalhöyük the dead were buried under the platforms of the houses where the living slept
events.text: A grandmother has died. As always, she will be buried under the sleeping platform of her own house, so she stays with her family.

events.title: The Mountain Breathes Fire
events.source: Hasan Dağ erupted around 6900 BCE, within the lifetime of Çatalhöyük
events.text: The twin mountain on the horizon is smoking and glowing at night. A painter climbs to the roofs to watch, and wants to paint it on the wall above the town's houses.

options.label: Paint the mountain
options.result: The houses of the town, row on row, and above them the mountain spitting fire: the first picture of a place.

events.title: No House Bigger Than Another
events.source: Ian Hodder found little sign of rank at Çatalhöyük: houses were similar in size, and men and women ate much the same food
events.text: A family has grown rich in grain and wants to build a house twice as big as the others. The neighbours are unhappy.

options.label: All houses alike
options.result: The family builds a house like everyone else's, and shares its grain at the feast.

options.label: Let them build big
options.result: The big house rises over the rooftops. Things will be different now.

tales.name: The Vultures and the Headless
tales.source: A story made up around the vulture paintings of Çatalhöyük
tales.text: On the wall of the old house, great vultures with spread wings stoop over small headless people. The grandmothers say: they are not eating the dead, they are lifting them, carrying the body to the sky while the head stays home with us under the floor.
tales.moral: the dead are both gone and here

tales.name: Why We Walk on the Roofs
tales.source: A story made up around the roof-entry houses
tales.text: When the first families came to the plain, each built its house touching its neighbour's, so that no one would ever be left outside. There was no room for paths, so they walked on the roofs, and the whole town became one house with many rooms.
tales.moral: close neighbours keep each other safe

tales.name: The Lady Between the Leopards
tales.source: A story made up around the Seated Woman figurine
tales.text: The oldest woman of the town was so wise that even leopards lay down beside her. When she sat in the grain bin to rest, the grain never ran out. When she died, the people made her in clay and kept her among the grain.

tales.name: The Whitening
tales.source: A story made up around the yearly replastering of houses
tales.text: Every spring the whole town whitens its walls. The old paintings disappear under fresh clay, and each family paints something new: a bull, a hand, a leopard, the mountain. Then everyone climbs to the roofs to eat together in the sun.
